taxable.name: Taxable brokerage
taxable.detail: Gains, interest and distributions are taxed as they come.

traditional.name: Tax-deferred
traditional.detail: Traditional IRA or 401(k): taxed as income on withdrawal.

roth.name: Roth
roth.detail: Roth IRA or Roth 401(k): qualified withdrawals are untaxed.

stacked.name: Stacked funds
stacked.detail: Funds that hold stocks and add a diversifier with futures. No loan and no margin call.

margin.name: Margin loan
margin.detail: Borrowed from the broker. It costs more and can be called.

growth.name: Growth, untouched for 10 years or more
growth.detail: Retirement that is still far off.

taxable: Both ways of holding more than 100% of capital are open in this account: funds that carry the exposure inside, or a margin loan.

Taxes are not modelled. Stock index funds defer most of their gain until sold. The diversifiers are taxed harder: Treasury interest is ordinary income (free of state tax), funds holding gold bullion are taxed as collectibles, and funds that use futures pay out most of their return as taxable distributions.
The replay rebalances every month. In this account a sale can realise a gain.
traditional: A retirement account cannot take a margin loan. Exposure above 100% of capital can only come from funds that carry it inside.
Nothing is taxed until withdrawal, and withdrawals are taxed as ordinary income whatever was held. No holding is tax-favoured over another, and rebalancing costs no tax.
roth: A retirement account cannot take a margin loan. Exposure above 100% of capital can only come from funds that carry it inside.
Qualified withdrawals are untaxed. No holding is tax-favoured over another, and rebalancing costs no tax.
